minimaxh3.ptx

Hand-written PTX kernels for MiniMax-H3 text-to-audio-video generation: a prompt becomes a short video with a stereo soundtrack. The whole file, as the engine loads it: each kernel and device function in a card with its parameters, resources and cross references, then its code. Every label, parameter, array and function name links to its definition; hover a register to see each of its uses in that function, click it to keep them marked.

lines 1–38
minimaxh3.ptx - hand-written PTX kernels for MiniMax-H3 text-to-audio-video generation: a prompt becomes a short video with a stereo soundtrack. The host (minimaxh3.c) runs four networks, one after the other: text encoder (Qwen3-VL-32B language model cut to 50 layers, width 5120, 64 query / 8 key-value heads of 128, causal, no final norm): h = embed(tokens); per layer: h += o(attn(rope(norm(qkv(rms(h)))))) h += down(swiglu(gate|up(rms(h)))) rms_mod, dequant_q4k / q6k + gemm_f16, qk_norm_rope, attn_d128 (causal, grouped), swiglu diffusion transformer (50 blocks + 2 token-refiner blocks, width 5376, 56 heads of 128): one packed sequence [text | audio L | audio R | video] with 3-D RoPE on 96 of each head's 128 dims; every block modulates its norms with AdaLN vectors chosen per token by (timestep, modality): x += gate1 * out(attn(qk_norm_rope(qkv(rms(x) * (1 + scale1) + shift1)))) x += gate2 * fc2(swiglu(fc1(rms(x) * (1 + scale2) + shift2))) adaln, rms_mod, gemm_f16 (mode 5: gated residual), qk_norm_rope, attn_d128, swiglu, linear_f32 video VAE decoder (a 36-layer ViT, width 2048, 32 heads of 64, RoPE on 48 dims): one latent token -> a 4 x 16 x 16 x 3 block of pixels, decoded in overlapping chunks of 7 latent frames and 256-pixel tiles rms_mod, gemm_f16, qk_norm_rope, attn_d64, layernorm audio VAE decoder (BigVGAN: 7 transposed convolutions, x800 in all, with anti-aliased SnakeBeta residual blocks): 40 latents/s -> 32 kHz, per channel im2col1d + gemm_f16, col2im_t, aa_snake, axpby Big matrices stay in their GGUF formats on the GPU (Q4_K, Q6_K) and are expanded to f16 one slice of rows at a time just before their GEMM; every matrix product is an f16 tensor-core mma with f32 accumulation. The residual streams, norms, softmax statistics and small heads stay f32. Activations are row-major [tokens][channels] (audio: [time][channels]).

dequant_q4k

lines 121–228
Kernel: dequant_q4k Q4_K blocks -> f16 values (a matrix slice, row-major) Block (144 bytes, 256 values = 8 sub-blocks of 32): f16 d, f16 dmin, u8 scales[12] (a 6-bit scale and min per sub-block), u8 qs[128]. Sub-block j: w = d * sc_j * q - dmin * m_j, q = nibble (j & 1) of qs[32 (j / 2) + l]; (sc_j, m_j) as ggml's get_scale_min_k4: for j < 4 the low 6 bits of scales[j] and scales[j + 4], else 4 bits of scales[j + 4] plus the top 2 bits of scales[j - 4] (scale) / scales[j] (min). One thread per sub-block, grid-stride; writes 32 halves.

dequant_q6k

lines 240–347
Kernel: dequant_q6k Q6_K blocks -> f16 values Block (210 bytes, 256 values): u8 ql[128], u8 qh[64], i8 scales[16], f16 d. Half n (values 128 n ..) uses ql[64 n ..], qh[32 n ..], scales[8 n ..]; its value 32 k + l (k < 4, l < 32) is q = (nibble (k >> 1) of ql[l + 32 (k & 1)]) | (bits 2k, 2k+1 of qh[l]) << 4, w = d * scales[l / 16 + 2 k] * (q - 32). One thread per 16 values (half n, quarter k, l from 16 il), grid-stride. 210-byte blocks are only 2-byte aligned: bytes are read one by one.

rms_mod

lines 357–504
Kernel: rms_mod per row: v = x / sqrt(mean(x^2) + eps) [* w], then the AdaLN modulation v + v * scale[s] + shift[s] of the row's segment s = seg[row] (s = 0 without seg), and the outputs: y16 = v * oscale (f16) and/or y32 = v (f32). w, shift/scale, seg, y16, y32 may each be 0. shift and scale rows are mstride elements apart per segment. One warp per row (n % 128 == 0), 8 rows per 256-thread block.

qk_norm_rope

lines 649–821
Kernel: qk_norm_rope in place on a fused projection (f16 [rows][ld]): every q head (nq of them, at columns qoff + h*hstride) and k head (nk, at koff + h*hstride) gets an RMS norm over its D values (times qw / kw when given), then a rotary embedding of its first `rot` dims in rotate-half form: dim i < rot/2 pairs with i + rot/2 and both turn by angle a_i of the row's table cs (f32 [rows][rot/2][2] cos, sin): x'_i = x_i c - x_(i+rot/2) s, x'_(i+rot/2) = x_i s + x_(i+rot/2) c. Dims >= rot keep their values (partial rotary). cs = 0: no rotation. One warp per (row, head), D / 32 values per lane (D = 64 or 128); the partner of a lane's dims sits rot/2 / (D/32) lanes away (shfl).

swiglu

lines 829–907
Kernel: swiglu out[r][j] = silu(a) * b * so with a = in[r][j] * si, b = in[r][F + j] * si (gate half first, then the up half, as ggml_swiglu splits one projection). si and so undo / apply the 1/128 scaling that keeps f16 activations in range. One thread per output pair, grid-stride.

kernel

adaln

lines 918–1000
Kernel: adaln the AdaLN modulation vectors of every block for every timestep in the sequence: out[(l R + r) J + j] = b[l J + j] + sum_i W[l J + j][i] * temb[r][i] (8 inputs: the interpolated row of the adaln_t_table curve). W and b f16, all blocks back to back. Block l's rows are [timestep r][modality m][6][hidden] (shift, scale, gate of attention, then of the MLP), so (r, m) is one row of 6 * hidden values. One thread per (l, j), grid-stride.

aa_snake

lines 1372–1479
Kernel: aa_snake BigVGAN's anti-aliased SnakeBeta activation, per channel (time-major f32 [L][ld], C channels): 1. upsample x2: replicate-pad x by 5, transposed conv (stride 2) with the 12-tap filter up, keep samples 15 .. 15 + 2L: u[n] = sum_i x[clamp(i - 5)] up[n + 15 - 2 i] 2. snake: u + sin(u e^alpha)^2 / (e^beta + 1e-9) 3. downsample x2: replicate-pad u by 5 / 6, 12-tap filter dn, stride 2: y[t] = sum_j dn[j] u[clamp(2 t + j - 5)] so each output needs 12 upsampled samples of 6 taps each. One thread per (t, c), grid-stride.

gemm_f16

lines 1502–1846
Kernel: gemm_f16 C[M][N] = A[M][K] . B[N][K]^T + bias, with an epilogue A: f16 activations [M][K] (rows readable up to M rounded up to 128), B: f16 weights [N][K] (a PyTorch Linear weight as stored), bias f32 [N] or 0. Needs N % 128 == 0 and K % 32 == 0. Block tile 128 x 128, k-tile 32; 256 threads = 8 warps as 2 (rows) x 4 (cols), each warp 64 x 32 = 4 x 4 mma.m16n8k16 tiles (f16 in, f32 acc). Tiles go global -> shared with cp.async in a 3-stage ring (two k-tiles in flight while one is computed) and shared -> registers with ldmatrix. Shared rows are 64 bytes (4 chunks of 8 halves); chunk c of row r is stored at chunk c ^ ((r >> 1) & 3) so that the 8 row addresses of every ldmatrix phase hit 8 different 16-byte bank groups. mode (the epilogue, per pair of adjacent outputs v = acc * alpha + bias; alpha undoes an input scaled to keep f16 in range, or scales the output): 0 C f32 = v 1 C f16 = v 4 C f32 += v 5 C f32 += v * gate[s][col], s = seg[row] (seg u8 [M], or s = 0 when seg is 0): the gated residual of an AdaLN block, where every row uses the gate of its segment (text, audio or video tokens) grid (N / 128, ceil(M / 128)), block 256. C row stride ldc, gate row stride gld (elements).

attn_d128

lines 1865–2843
Kernel: attn_d128 O = softmax(Q K^T * scale) V for every head, reading Q, K and V where the fused projection left them: token t's q of head h at columns qoff + h*hstride .. +128 of row t of qkv (f16 [N][ld]), its k and v at koff / voff + (h / group)*hstride (group > 1: grouped-query attention). 128-dim heads, 64 queries per block (4 warps x 16 rows), key tiles of 32. Key tiles go to shared memory with cp.async, two buffers (the next tile loads while this one is used); rows past N are zero-filled (cp.async with src-size 0) and masked. Shared rows are 256 bytes (16 chunks of 16): chunk c of row r is stored at chunk c ^ (r & 7). S = Q K^T and O += P V are mma.m16n8k16 (f16 in, f32 acc); the softmax is the online one in base 2 (scores times scale * log2(e), exponentials with ex2). P never leaves registers: the S accumulators of two adjacent 8-key tiles are the A fragment of one 16-key mma step. causal != 0: key <= query. The Q tile is staged in the second buffer before the first prefetch. grid (ceil(N / 64), H), block 128. O f16 [N][ldo], head h at h*128.

attn_d64

lines 2862–3834
Kernel: attn_d64 O = softmax(Q K^T * scale) V for every head, reading Q, K and V where the fused projection left them: token t's q of head h at columns qoff + h*hstride .. +64 of row t of qkv (f16 [N][ld]), its k and v at koff / voff + (h / group)*hstride (group > 1: grouped-query attention). 64-dim heads, 64 queries per block (4 warps x 16 rows), key tiles of 64. Key tiles go to shared memory with cp.async, two buffers (the next tile loads while this one is used); rows past N are zero-filled (cp.async with src-size 0) and masked. Shared rows are 128 bytes (8 chunks of 16): chunk c of row r is stored at chunk c ^ (r & 7). S = Q K^T and O += P V are mma.m16n8k16 (f16 in, f32 acc); the softmax is the online one in base 2 (scores times scale * log2(e), exponentials with ex2). P never leaves registers: the S accumulators of two adjacent 8-key tiles are the A fragment of one 16-key mma step. causal != 0: key <= query. The Q tile is staged in the second buffer before the first prefetch. grid (ceil(N / 64), H), block 128. O f16 [N][ldo], head h at h*64.
